steps: Cook the rice and warm the beans (refried or black), or use pre-cooked leftovers of each.
Warm the flour tortillas briefly on a dry pan or in the microwave until pliable.
Spread beans, rice, grated cheddar and a spoonful of salsa across the centre of each tortilla.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly into a burrito.
Wrap each burrito individually in foil and freeze flat.
To serve, unwrap and reheat from frozen in the microwave for about 3 minutes, turning once, until piping hot throughout.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cube the sweet potato and press-dry the tofu, then toss each separately in oil and seasoning.
Roast the sweet potato and tofu on separate trays for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until the sweet potato is tender and the tofu is golden.
Cook the quinoa according to the packet instructions and leave to cool.
Slice the peppers and onion thinly and mix with the sweetcorn (sauté briefly if you prefer them softened).
Lay a whole-wheat tortilla flat and fill with the quinoa, roasted sweet potato, tofu, and pepper-onion-corn mix.
Fold in the sides, roll tightly, wrap in foil and refrigerate until ready to eat.
Spoon the Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Scatter over the mixed berries and granola.
Drizzle with honey and serve immediately.
Preheat the oven to 175°C and line a muffin tin with paper cases.
Combine the almond meal, oats, cinnamon, baking soda and salt in a bowl; in a separate bowl whisk the eggs with the grated carrot, honey and melted butter.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry until just combined, then divide the batter among the muffin cases.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until browned on top and a knife inserted in the centre comes out clean; cool completely, then freeze extras for later.
To serve, thaw or reheat 2 muffins and plate alongside the Greek yogurt and mixed berries.
Hard-boil the eggs (10-12 minutes), then cool and peel.
Slice the cheese and cut the carrot sticks.
Arrange the eggs, cheese, edamame, crackers, apple and carrot sticks on a plate.
Serve with the hummus for dipping.
Cook the sticky white rice and keep it warm.
Scramble the eggs in a lightly oiled pan with the diced ham or bacon until just set.
Stir the egg-ham mixture, parmesan and tamari through the warm rice until evenly combined.
Press the mixture firmly into a lined tray to about 2cm thick.
Let cool, then cut into 6 squares and wrap each individually in foil.
Scramble the egg in a small non-stick pan with a little of the olive oil until just set.
In a bowl, combine the warm cooked sushi rice, scrambled egg, parmesan and a pinch of salt.
Mix in the remaining olive oil until the rice holds together when pressed.
Press the mixture into a lined tray to an even thickness and leave to firm up for a few minutes.
Cut into 8 squares and wrap individually for the ride.
Cook the sushi rice with a dash of salt (or use pre-cooked) and transfer to a bowl while still warm.
Stir in the grated apple, beaten egg and half the brown sugar until evenly combined.
Spread the mixture evenly into a lined baking tray.
Sprinkle the remaining brown sugar and cinnamon over the top.
Let set for a few minutes, then cut into 8 squares and wrap individually.
Sauté the diced ham, bell pepper and onion in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat until the onion is translucent.
Pour in the beaten egg and cook, stirring, until just set.
Stir the egg mixture and grated cheddar through the warm cooked rice until evenly combined.
Press the mixture into a lined tray and leave to firm up for a few minutes.
Cut into 8 squares and wrap individually.
Cook the white rice with a pinch of salt (or use pre-cooked) and keep it warm.
Stir the maple syrup and beaten egg into the warm rice until well combined, then fold in the chopped dark chocolate.
Spoon the mixture into a zip-lock bag or lined tray, flatten evenly, and chill in the fridge until firm, ideally overnight.
Turn out onto a board and cut into 8 squares.
Wrap the squares individually in foil and keep refrigerated until needed.
Boil the risotto rice in water with the coconut oil, coconut palm sugar and cinnamon until all the water has been absorbed.
Fold the cream cheese into the rice while it's still warm.
Mix in the agave syrup and blend thoroughly.
Pour into a large zip-lock bag, flatten to smooth out the air, and leave to cool on a flat tray.
Once cool, transfer to the fridge and chill overnight.
Cut the chilled rice into squares and wrap individually in foil.
Boil the pudding rice in water with the coconut milk, turn down the heat, cover and simmer, stirring regularly, until the rice is soft and the liquid has been absorbed.
Stir in the brown sugar and cinnamon.
Transfer to a container lined with cling film, press flat, seal and refrigerate overnight.
Turn out and cut into 8 squares.
Wrap in foil for easy transport.
Preheat the oven to 170°C (Gas Mark 3).
Blend all the ingredients except the butter and cherries.
Add the melted butter while blending on a low-to-medium speed.
Grease the muffin tins and sprinkle them with almond flour.
Spoon the batter into the tins, filling each about 2.5-3cm deep, and press the cherries gently into the batter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, rotating the tins once or twice, until golden brown and firm.
Combine the rolled oats, peanut butter, honey, ground flax and dried fruit in a bowl until evenly mixed.
If the mixture is too dry to hold together, stir in a splash of water or a little extra honey.
Roll into small balls, about a tablespoon each.
Chill in the fridge for at least 15 minutes to firm up before packing.
